title: coolify-mcp connection registry (v1)
$comment: HAND-WRITTEN MIRROR of connectionSchema/configFileSchema in src/config/schema.ts. zod-to-json-schema is deliberately not a dependency, so the two are kept in sync by a parity test that feeds the same fixtures to both: any property, default, bound or pattern changed in schema.ts must be changed here in the same commit. This file is published in the npm package (see package.json files[]) and is what a user's $schema key points at.

$schema.description: Points at this file so editors can validate and autocomplete the registry.

defaultConnection.description: Connection used when a tool call does not name one. $COOLIFY_CONNECTION overrides it. With exactly one connection it is unnecessary; with several and none designated, tools require an explicit instance.

extends.description: Path to a base registry file, resolved relative to this file ('~/' is expanded). Exactly one level: the base file may not itself extend another. A name defined in both files replaces the base entry whole — there is no field-level merge.

connections.description: A connection is (baseUrl, token). A Coolify token is bound to the team that was active when it was created, so a second team is a second token, which is a second connection — the same baseUrl may appear more than once.

connectionName.description: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter or digit, 31 characters max. The name maps to env vars by uppercasing and replacing - with _: 'acme-ops' <-> COOLIFY_API_TOKEN_ACME_OPS.

connection.$comment: There is no 'token' property, and additionalProperties is false, so a literal credential here is a schema validation error rather than a discouraged option. This is the enforcement mechanism, not documentation.
connection.description: coolify-mcp never stores credentials in config files. Point at a credential with tokenEnv, tokenCommand or tokenKeychain, or set none of them and $COOLIFY_API_TOKEN_<NAME> is read by convention.

baseUrl.description: Root URL of the Coolify instance, e.g. https://coolify.example.com. Must not embed credentials (https://user:pass@host is rejected).

label.description: Human label shown in doctor output and error messages.

tokenEnv.description: Name of the environment variable holding the API token.

tokenCommand.description: Argv array executed WITHOUT a shell; trimmed stdout is the token. No string splitting, no interpolation. Example: ["op", "read", "op://Infra/coolify/credential"].

tokenKeychain.description: Platform credential store: macOS `security find-generic-password`, Linux `secret-tool lookup`, Windows user-scoped DPAPI ciphertext at %LOCALAPPDATA%\coolify-mcp\credentials.dat (not Credential Manager — no first-party CLI returns a generic credential's secret).

readOnly.description: Refuse every write and destructive operation on this connection regardless of token scope. $COOLIFY_READ_ONLY=true forces this on for all connections; it can only tighten, never loosen.

allowDestructive.description: Per-connection override of $COOLIFY_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE. Defaults to that flag. In practice it can only narrow: the destructive tool is registered from the global flag, so true here grants nothing on a server where the flag is off.

insecureTLS.description: Accept self-signed certificates. For homelab instances only — it disables certificate verification for this connection.

allOf.$comment: At most one token source: two sources means two answers to 'where is the token' and no rule for which wins.
